findings.issue: Headline table and AC-5 row use '~5.5–7.9k rec/s @300k' band; the committed measurements.json records 5,454 rec/s, which is marginally below 5,500 (the band's lower end). The actual value IS stated correctly in §3 ('the committed measurements.json records the last run at 5,454 rec/s'), but the headline table creates a slight inconsistency. Not blocking — the traceability note in §3 correctly explains the band spans multiple runs.
findings.suggestion: Change headline band to '~5.5–7.9k' → '~5.5k–7.9k (committed run: 5,454 rec/s)' or adjust the lower bound to '~5.4k–7.9k' to include the committed value without ambiguity.

findings.issue: FF-SMOKE-JSON calls 'run.sh measure' after a small-N (1000) seed run, which overwrites the Flowable EngineResult in measurements.json with smoke-level data. This is exactly the 'known gнильца' acknowledged in the BUILD commit (6d5aebc: 'Flowable EngineResult restored to N=300k after smoke'). The committed measurements.json is correct (N=300000), but running fitness.sh on a live Docker environment will silently clobber the full-run measurements for the tested engine. No git-safe guard (e.g. git stash/restore) is in place.
findings.suggestion: Add a note to fitness.sh (comment near FF-SMOKE-JSON) warning that the smoke run will overwrite the engine's EngineResult in measurements.json with N=1000 data, and that git checkout -- spikes/flowable-oss/measurements.json should be run after fitness.sh to restore the full-run evidence. Alternatively, have FF-SMOKE-JSON write to a separate measurements.smoke.json so the full-run measurements.json is never touched by the smoke.
